scope: US deucrictibant IR/XR public adoption evidence; no valuation or Monte Carlo
schema_note: Each observation inherits source date, geography and population through source_id; null means unavailable or not applicable, never zero. Observed means source-reported, not independently validated. Derived includes our arithmetic or source-estimated values; neither is automatically a PHVS forecast.

S1.title: BioCryst January 2026 JPM presentation
S1.independence: Slide 8 persistence recycles S2; not a second cohort

S2.title: Zuraw et al. Adherence and persistence among patients with HAE receiving LTP in the US
S2.population: 357 linked EHR/claims patients aged >=12; initiated Jun 22 2017–Sep 12 2023; >=12 months enrollment before and after; hierarchical reverse-approval cohort assignment
S2.independence: BioCryst-affiliated authors; S1 repeats results. Patient overlap with other databases unknown.

S3.title: O’Connor et al. LTP compliance and impact on on-demand treatment claims
S3.population: 328 commercially insured IQVIA PharMetrics Plus patients; Jan 2016–Sep 2023; >=6 months pre-index and >=12 post; first non-androgen LTP claim; multiple index LTP and claims outliers excluded
S3.independence: KalVista-associated study and funded writing; potential subsequent publication is not independent

S4.title: Real-world treatment patterns and clinical burden of patients with HAE treated with LTP
S4.population: 499 Komodo claims patients aged >=12; index Jan 2021–Jan 2024; >=12 months baseline and >=30 days follow-up; pharmacy-fill requirement; 257 Orladeyo,185 Takhzyro,57 Haegarda
S4.independence: Ionis funded; overlaps with other claims populations cannot be ruled out

S5.title: PIONEER-HAE: LTP real-world treatment patterns in selected US allergy clinics
S5.population: 179 type I/II patients in CIIC practices observed Apr 2021–Mar 2024; historical index therapies 2009–2024; >=180 days before and after index
S5.independence: Ionis funded; separate setting from claims; no proof of patient independence

S6.title: Patient Preferences for LTP in HAE: A Discrete-Choice Experiment
S6.population: 250 self-reported adult HAE respondents recruited through advocacy group; 81.6% female,85.2% white; selected voluntary sample
S6.independence: Ionis funded, RTI conducted; not observed dispensing

S8.title: 2025 US treated-HAE claims prevalence study
S8.population: 2020 projection from IQVIA, continuous enrollment, diagnosis algorithm plus >=1 HAE drug claim
S8.source_type: original observational projection; prior verified extraction retained
S8.independence: Not re-extracted this pass; access blocked

S9.title: KalVista January 2026 corporate update
S9.independence: Different definition and date from S8; not independent validation

S10.title: KalVista March 25 2026 commercial update
S10.source_type: company disclosure; prior verified extraction retained
S10.independence: Forms, prescriptions and revenue are not separate confirmation of paid-patient count

observations.definition: All on-therapy patients, including QuickStart, paid and PAP
observations.limitation: Not exact count, paid count or October 2026 stock; age eligibility requires alignment
Do not divide A01 by A02 for persistence or subtract for discontinued patients; both are lower bounds and cohort ages differ

observations.denominator: On-therapy patients excluding QuickStart; count undisclosed
observations.limitation: Not new-start conversion, denial rate or payer net price; cannot multiply by A01
Rounded; numerator unavailable. Not causal product ranking or stable-incumbent annual retention

observations.definition: Mean days covered divided by observation days
observations.limitation: PDC is not persistence or paid conversion

observations.definition: >=1 claim for a different LTP, including patients who later return
observations.limitation: Not share switching to PHVS, not incumbent stable-user hazard, not paid persistent destination adoption

observations.definition: Claims-recorded rescue dispensing among LTP initiators
observations.model_use: Evidence prevention and rescue demand overlap
observations.limitation: Absence of claim does not prove absence of attacks or available stock

observations.observation_period: Pre-index year (annualized if <364 days available) and 12 months post
observations.limitation: Not actual consumed attacks; stocking, wastage, free supply and product dosing differ

observations.definition: No gap >60 days for lanadelumab or >30 days for other LTP
observations.limitation: Selected post-index subgroup; confounding prevents causal interpretation

observations.definition: Any different LTP claim during follow-up
observations.limitation: Increase not statistically significant (reported P=0.12); not proof switching causes attacks

observations.denominator: 499 starting patients; KM risk set varies
observations.definition: Failure at gap >=90 days or switch; censor at follow-up end
observations.limitation: Do not average with 45-day-gap S2; different population and definition

observations.observation_period: Variable follow-up; data availability mean 18.0 months
observations.limitation: Not a 12-month switching rate; on-treatment mean 11.3 months is a different clock

observations.observation_period: Variable follow-up; data availability mean 18.0 months
observations.limitation: Not annualized or evidence of permanent cessation; do not treat index-drug shares as market shares

observations.observation_period: Variable historical treatment durations; index 2009–2024, registry observation 2021–2024
observations.limitation: Not a one-year rate; differing time axes and treatment-entry eras

observations.model_use: Allow switch, restart and unknown/no-record destinations
observations.limitation: No subsequent record does not prove acute-only; not a full annual transition matrix

observations.observation_period: At cessation; reasons available in 76/83 cases
observations.definition: Recorded nonexclusive reasons among discontinuers with known reasons
observations.model_use: Mechanism evidence for dissatisfaction and access pathways
observations.limitation: Not prevalence among all patients; rounded, subjective and nonexclusive

observations.metric: Median berotralstat time to cessation among discontinuers
observations.observation_period: Historical treatment episodes ending in cessation
observations.limitation: NOT median persistence among all berotralstat users; do not input to retention curve

observations.observation_period: Cross-sectional survey; exact field dates not recovered
observations.model_use: Qualitative constraint on universal dissatisfaction thesis
observations.limitation: Everyone else is not necessarily dissatisfied; selected survey cannot size national segments

observations.definition: Stated openness to new medication with preferred administration
observations.limitation: Not observed switching, coverage or paid persistence

observations.model_use: Support heterogeneous response to efficacy and burden
observations.limitation: No new fitting here; do not copy as US market weights

observations.definition: Relative importance over the attribute levels tested
observations.limitation: Not sales weights or efficacy-to-switching coefficients

observations.definition: Two claims-algorithm definitions of treated HAE
observations.limitation: Not current TAM confidence interval, untreated prevalence or eligible PHVS population
Different definition/year from A22; method not independently validated
Not paid patients or mature active users; no public aligned paid-conversion cohort
Different geography/date from A24; cannot infer conversion by division
Announcement, not independent completion verification; historical Optime-only records may miss subsequent continuation

unknown_inputs.missing: Aligned date, age/subtype and coverage for oral, injectable, other-prevention and acute-only pools
unknown_inputs.scenario_requirement: Do not make the three requested groups exhaustive by discarding older oral prevention or uncertain records

unknown_inputs.input: New diagnoses and first prevention starts
unknown_inputs.missing: Incidence distinguished from newly observed claims, with lookback and prior channel capture

unknown_inputs.input: Paid persistent switching to PHVS by previous therapy/control
unknown_inputs.missing: Stable and dissatisfied incumbent denominators; competing destination therapies; first paid fill and persistence

unknown_inputs.input: First-paid-fill delay, abandonment and bridge conversion
unknown_inputs.missing: Start-cohort dates and hub/SP adjudication events; mature paid share cannot substitute

unknown_inputs.input: Acute treated-attack fraction, doses/attack and product choice
unknown_inputs.missing: Linked attack diary and dispense records, stratified by preventive treatment

unknown_inputs.input: Initial rescue stocking and expiry replacement
unknown_inputs.missing: Days/quantities dispensed, inventory use/replacement reason and follow-up; refills do not imply consumption

unknown_inputs.input: PHVS net price and benefit-weighted access
unknown_inputs.missing: Commercial terms and patient-weighted policy mapping; no universal payer or second-oral discount

dependencies: XR uptake -> fewer residual attacks -> less IR consumption; rescue ownership remains distinct
Disease control -> dissatisfaction, switching and rescue demand
Access/net contracting -> paid conversion, delay, abandonment and net price
Persistence -> paid treatment months and acute consumption
Source regimen -> early discontinuation and destination competition; stable survivors differ from new initiators
IR effectiveness and preference -> willingness to initiate XR; same-drug combined use remains a clinical/label question
